claims.text: A zirconia-based ceramic coating applied to dipping and plating components will protect them from erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
Mild steel is representative of the standard uncoated substrate material used for rollers and guide plates.
The zirconia-based ceramic coating should be applied to component surfaces before exposure to molten aluminum.
Hot-dip aluminum plating involves exposure to liquid aluminum at temperatures above its melting point.
The melting point of aluminum is approximately 660°C.
The proposed ceramic coating has a dense, low-porosity microstructure.
A dense, low-porosity coating microstructure resists aluminum penetration and chemical attack.
Zirconia is chemically inert toward high-temperature liquid aluminum.
Zirconia is thermally stable under the proposed hot-dip aluminum plating conditions.
The zirconia coating forms a barrier that prevents direct contact between the substrate and liquid aluminum.
Preventing direct substrate–aluminum contact reduces chemical erosion and physical degradation.
Zirconia-coated components will have significantly lower corrosion rates than untreated components.
Zirconia-coated components will exhibit less aluminum penetration than untreated components.
Zirconia-coated components will have a notably longer service life than untreated components.
Uncoated components undergo rapid corrosion because of direct exposure to high-temperature liquid aluminum.
Coating adhesion, thermal cycling, mechanical stress, and spallation can limit coating effectiveness.
No direct evidence or experimental data are provided for zirconia coatings in this specific hot-dip aluminum plating environment.
